arxiv-2202-03949.title: Systematically and efficiently improving k k -means initialization by pairwise-nearest-neighbor smoothing
arxiv-2202-03949.creator: Carlo Baldassi carlo.baldassi@unibocconi.it
arxiv-2202-03949.description: Abstract We present a meta-method for initializing (seeding) the k k -means clustering algorithm called PNN-smoothing. It consists in splitting a given dataset into J J random subsets, clustering each of them individually, and merging the resulting clusterings with the pairwise-nearest-neighbor (PNN) method.

arxiv-2207-01340.title: How centralized is decentralized? Comparison of wealth distribution in coins and tokens
arxiv-2207-01340.creator: Bartosz Kuśmierz, Roman Overko
arxiv-2207-01340.description: Abstract Rapidly growing distributed ledger technologies (DLTs) have recently received attention among researchers in both industry and academia. While a lot of existing analysis (mainly) of the Bitcoin and Ethereum networks is available, the lack of measurements for other crypto projects is observed. This article addresses questions about tokenomics and wealth distributions in cryptocurrencies.

arxiv-2208-12097.title: Training a T5 Using Lab-sized Resources
arxiv-2208-12097.creator: Manuel R. Ciosici, Leon Derczynski
arxiv-2208-12097.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Manuel R. Ciosici, Leon Derczynski. Training large neural language models on large datasets is resource- and time-intensive. These requirements create a barrier to entry, where those with fewer resources cannot build competitive models. This paper presents various techniques for making it possible to (a) train a large language model using resources that a modest research lab might have, and (b) train it in a reasonable amount of time.

arxiv-2312-10495.title: Computing Optimal Joint Chance Constrained Control Policies
arxiv-2312-10495.creator: Niklas Schmid, Marta Fochesato, Sarah H.Q. Li, Tobias Sutter, John Lygeros
arxiv-2312-10495.description: Abstract We consider the problem of optimally controlling stochastic, Markovian systems subject to joint chance constraints over a finite-time horizon. For such problems, standard Dynamic Programming is inapplicable due to the time correlation of the joint chance constraints, which calls for non-Markovian, and possibly stochastic, policies.

arxiv-2402-16602.title: Rethinking Negative Instances for Generative Named Entity Recognition
arxiv-2402-16602.creator: Yuyang Ding, Juntao Li, Pinzheng Wang, Zecheng Tang, Bowen Yan, Min Zhang
arxiv-2402-16602.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities for generalizing in unseen tasks. In the Named Entity Recognition (NER) task, recent advancements have seen the remarkable improvement of LLMs in a broad range of entity domains via instruction tuning, by adopting entity-centric schema.

arxiv-2410-07920.title: Post-Training Quantization in Brain-Computer Interfaces based on Event-Related Potential Detection
arxiv-2410-07920.creator: Hubert Cecotti, Dalvir Dhaliwal, Hardip Singh, Yogesh Kumar Meena
arxiv-2410-07920.description: Abstract Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a technique used to optimize and reduce the memory footprint and computational requirements of machine learning models. It has been used primarily for neural networks. For Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) that are fully portable and usable in various situations, it is necessary to provide approaches that are lightweight for storage and computation.

arxiv-2501-00131.title: Fermi-ball in a multicomponent dark matter framework and its gravitational wave signatures
arxiv-2501-00131.creator: Nabarun Chakrabarty, Indrani Chakraborty, Himadri Roy
arxiv-2501-00131.description: Abstract It has been known that under-abundant dark matter density of an inert doublet can be replenished by an additional dark matter component, say, a fermion. We find that such a scenario can lead to the formation of stable Fermi-balls through coexisting minima of the finite temperature scalar potential.

arxiv-2501-17166.title: Optimizing Carbon Footprint in ICT through Swarm Intelligence with Algorithmic Complexity
arxiv-2501-17166.creator: Nikitas Gerolimos, Vasileios Alevizos, Sabrina Edralin, Clark Xu, Akebu Simasiku, Georgios Priniotakis, George A. Papakostas, Zongliang Yue
arxiv-2501-17166.description: Abstract Global emissions from fossil fuel combustion and cement production were recorded in 2022, signaling a resurgence to pre-pandemic levels and providing an apodictic indication that emission peaks have not yet been achieved. Significant contributions to this upward trend are made by the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) industry due to its substantial energy consumption.

britannica-1911-miller-samuel-freeman.description: Article 'Miller, Samuel Freeman' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. twelve he began to write verses. During the next few years he obtained employment as a journeyman mason in Edinburgh, Inverness and various other parts of Scotland.

Since most wastewater virus concentration methods were developed and validated for...

pmc-10690451.title: Assessment of a feed additive containing Enterococcus lactis NCIMB 11181 (Lactiferm®) for weaned piglets, calves for fattening and calves for rearing for the renewal of its authorisation (Chr. Hansen A/S)
pmc-10690451.creator: EFSA Panel on Additives and Products or Substances used in Animal Feed (FEEDAP), Vasileios Bampidis, Giovanna Azimonti, Maria de Lourdes Bastos, Henrik Christensen, Mojca Durjava, Birgit Dusemund, Maryline Kouba, Marta López‐Alonso, Secundino López Puente, Francesca Marcon, Baltasar Mayo, Alena Pech
pmc-10690451.description: Following a request from the European Commission, EFSA was asked to deliver a scientific opinion on the assessment of the application for renewal of the authorisation of Enterococcus lactis NCIMB 11181 (Lactiferm®) as a zootechnical additive for weaned piglets, calves for fattening and calves for rearing. The product under assessment is based on a strain originally identified as Enterococcus faecium.

pmc-10714607.title: The sixth Japanese meeting on biological function and evolution through interactions between hosts and transposable elements
pmc-10714607.creator: Kenji Ichiyanagi, Yoko Ikeda, Kuniaki Saito
pmc-10714607.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The sixth Japanese meeting on host–transposon interactions, titled “Biological Function and Evolution through Interactions between Hosts and Transposable Elements,” was held on August 24th and 25th, 2023, at the National Institute of Genetics as well as online.

pmc-10743113.title: Image Entropy-Based Interface Evaluation Method for Nuclear Power Plants
pmc-10743113.creator: Wenzhe Tang, Shanguang Chen, Yun Lin, Chengqi Xue, Amelia Carolina Sparavigna
pmc-10743113.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The digital interface is crucial for nuclear plant operators, influencing their decision-making significantly. However, evaluations of these interfaces often overlook users’ decision-making performance; lack established standards, typically occurring after the design phase; and are unsuitable for large-scale assessments. Recognizing the vital role of interface information, this paper built on our previous research and proposed a method tailored for nuclear power plant interfaces, utilizing image entropy to evaluate the impact of information on decision-making.

pmc-11390725.title: Analysis of phosphofructokinase-1 activity as affected by pH and ATP concentration
pmc-11390725.creator: Chengcheng Wang, Mackenzie J. Taylor, Chandler D. Stafford, David S. Dang, Sulaiman K. Matarneh, David E. Gerrard, Jinglu Tan
pmc-11390725.description: A key player in energy metabolism is phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK1) whose activity and behavior strongly influence glycolysis and thus have implications in many areas. In this research, PFK1 assays were performed to convert F6P and ATP into F-1,6-P and ADP for varied pH and ATP concentrations.

pmc-11487711.title: Circularly Polarized High-Harmonic Beams Carrying Self-Torque or Time-Dependent Orbital Angular Momentum
pmc-11487711.creator: Alba de las Heras, Julio San Román, Javier Serrano, Luis Plaja, Carlos Hernández-García
pmc-11487711.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In the rapidly evolving field of structured light, self-torque has been recently defined as an intrinsic property of light beams carrying time-dependent orbital angular momentum. In particular, extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) beams with self-torque, exhibiting a topological charge that continuously varies on the subfemtosecond time scale, are naturally produced in high-order harmonic generation (HHG) when driven by two time-delayed intense infrared vortex beams with different topological charges.

pmc-11492955.title: Evaluating the importance of rural internships to subsequent medical workforce distribution outcomes: an Australian cohort study
pmc-11492955.creator: Matthew R McGrail, Jordan Fox, Priya Martin
pmc-11492955.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the importance of rural internships to observed medical workforce distribution outcomes up to 8 years post-medical school.Design and settingCohort study of medical graduates of The University of Queensland (UQ), Australia.ParticipantsUQ graduates who were medical interns in Queensland’s public health system between 2014 and 2021 and observed working in Australia in 2022.

pmc-11650285.title: Concomitant epidural and longitudinal anterior spinal artery contrast spread in a lumbar transforaminal epidural steroid injection (TFESI)
pmc-11650285.creator: Philip J Koehler, Paul M Kitei, David S Stolzenberg, Elaine H Hatch
pmc-11650285.description: A 78-year-old female with a remote history of L3-4 decompression and fusion presented with several months of low back and radicular leg pain. MRI revealed moderate L2-L3 spinal canal stenosis, ligamentum flavum infolding, moderate bilateral foraminal stenosis, and a grade I retrolisthesis. A right sided L2-L3 TFESI was performed using multiplanar fluoroscopic imaging with a subpedicular supraneural approach.

pmc-12483666.title: Research note: Individual variability in early-life play and social behaviors of broiler chicks
pmc-12483666.creator: Alexandra Jackson, Denise Landers, Joseph Purswell, Bethany Baker-Cook
pmc-12483666.description: Play and social behaviors are important in behavioral development as they support neurodevelopment, social bonding, and skills development. The individual differences in performance of these behaviors in poultry are currently unknown. This study assessed individual variability of play and social behaviors in broiler chicks across the first week of life. Seventy-five chicks (25 birds/pen) were randomly placed in three pens.

pmc-12603817.title: Predicting bone metastasis and high-grade Gleason scores in prostate cancer: a retrospective study integrating clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging radiomics
pmc-12603817.creator: Yuling Yang, Bin Zou, Bowen Zheng, Yongfei Guo, Shuiquan Yu, Biwei Chen
pmc-12603817.description: BackgroundProstate cancer (PCa) is a common malignant tumor in older men, and bone metastasis is its most frequent form. Once bone metastasis occurs, survival drops sharply. The Gleason score is the standard tool for judging how aggressive the cancer is; men with high-risk disease face higher chances of treatment failure and death.

pmc-12619472.title: Baricitinib could improve the prognosis of anti-MDA5 antibody positive dermatomyositis associated interstitial lung disease
pmc-12619472.creator: Shuai Zhu, Shanshan Li, Lipu Shi, Tianshu Chu, Zhenguo Huang, Xin Lu, Guochun Wang, Yongpeng Ge
pmc-12619472.description: Background and objectiveCurrently, there are only a few effective treatments for anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody (anti-MDA5) positive dermatomyositis (DM)-associated interstitial lung disease (ILD). The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of baricitinib in patients with MDA5 + DM-ILD.

pmc-12874996.title: A comparison of borderline personality features and level of personality functioning in explaining mentalizing capacity
pmc-12874996.creator: Charlotte S. Zell, Kennedy M. Balzen, Joseph Boudreaux, Francesca Penner, Carla Sharp
pmc-12874996.description: BackgroundNumerous studies have demonstrated that the Alternative Model for Personality Disorders (AMPD) outperforms traditional categorical nosology (i.e., Section II) in predicting an array of salient clinical outcomes. However, despite the centrality of social-cognitive impairments in personality disorder, few studies have examined the superiority of the AMPD over Section II in predicting social-cognitive deficits.

pmc-13518923.title: Identification of moderate effect size genes in autism spectrum disorder through a novel gene pairing approach
pmc-13518923.creator: Madison Caballero, F Kyle Satterstrom, Silvia de Rubeis, Joseph D Buxbaum, Behrang Mahjani
pmc-13518923.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) arises from complex genetic and environmental factors, with inherited genetic variation playing a substantial role. This study introduces a novel approach to uncover moderate effect size (MES) risk genes in ASD, which individually do not meet the ASD liability threshold but contribute to risk when paired with another MES risk gene.

pmc-13632144.title: Secondary Prophylaxis of Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infections During Systemic Antibiotics with Vancomycin (SPORES-V): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13632144.creator: Connor Prosty, Alex Carignan, Adrienne K Chan, Yan Chen, Peter Daley, Nick Daneman, Christopher Kandel, Yves Longtin, Santiago Perez-Patrigeon, Terry Wuerz, James Cheaveau, Susy S Hota, Olusola Ogundipe, Theodore S Steiner, Jennifer L Y Tsang, Patrick Archambault, Marco Bergevin, James M Brophy, Gab
pmc-13632144.description: BackgroundClostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a prevalent, morbid, and expensive disease that recurs in approximately 25% of patients despite treatment. Re-exposure to systemic antibiotics is one of the strongest risk factors for recurrence. Observational evidence and two small randomized controlled trials suggest that secondary vancomycin prophylaxis during antibiotic re-exposure may prevent recurrences, but the current evidence is not definitive.

pmc-13676368.title: Association between Perioperative Blood Glucose Levels and Wound Complications in Diabetic Patients Undergoing Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13676368.creator: Tomohiro Yamada, Yu Yamato, Tomohiko Hasegawa, Go Yoshida, Tomohiro Banno, Hideyuki Arima, Shin Oe, Hiroki Ushirozako, Koihiro Ide, Yusuke Murakami, Yukihiro Matsuyama
pmc-13676368.description: Introduction Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is highly invasive and carries a substantial risk of postoperative wound complications, particularly in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM). Perioperative hyperglycemia is a known risk factor for surgical-site infection, but glucose thresholds specific to patients with diabetes and ASD remain unclear.
